script: Ballon d'Or ceremonies that caused the rules to be changed. A few years ago in October 2024, Rodri beat Vinícius Jr. for the Ballon d'Or by just 41 points, which was one of the tightest finishes in recent memory, and the result was supposed to be a surprise until the announcement because for the first time ever, France Football decided that the winner would not be told in advance. Prior to this, France Football typically let the winners know within a week of the award, yet this one was supposed to be kept a secret with a select few insiders knowing who won. But somehow the winner leaked, and Real Madrid found hours before the show that Vinícius lost. So the entire club, ranging from the president to the players, all refused to go and straight up skipped the ceremony. Millions of people watched an awards show where the runners-up club didn't even bother showing up. Then a few weeks later, Real Madrid's president, Florentino Pérez, gave a speech criticizing the voting system, saying journalists from smaller countries had too much influence over the result, and that made headlines everywhere. So for 2025, France Football doubled down on secrecy even further. The editor-in-chief, Vincent Garcia, said he was the only person who knew the winner, and the result was announced live on stage by Ronaldinho, which was the first time anyone found out Ousmane Dembelé had won. And now the standard rule is for France Football to protect the winner's identity at all costs until the announcement.
what_makes_it_work: Strong narrative hook about dramatic rule changes in football's biggest individual award.

Framing historical sports drama like a heist story with leaks and extreme secrecy.
